Article Title: Oil prices today: Brent holds above $100 as Iran-US attacks threaten deeper supply disruption
Article Text:
Oil hits $100.

Strait of Hormuz in focus

Fuel prices

add to pressure

Oil prices extended gains on Thursday, with Brent holding above $100 a barrel as escalating Iran-US attacks on shipping heightened concerns over further disruptions to Middle East crude supplies.Brent crude futures rose 0.1% to $101.34 a barrel by 0107 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 0.5% to $96.55.Brent settled $3.29, or 3.4%, higher at $101.21 a barrel on Wednesday after touching $101.58. WTI rose $3.02, or 3.25%, to $96.05. Both benchmarks closed at their highest levels since May 22.The gains came after Iran said it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz, while the United States sank five Iranian oil tankers. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps also warned that it would step up its response to further attacks.The Strait of Hormuz remains a key flashpoint for global energy markets. Nearly one-fifth of the world's oil supply passed through the strategic waterway before the war, but oil and gas flows through the strait have remained well below pre-war levels.Oil prices had mostly stayed below $100 a barrel since late May as traders expected the conflict to remain contained.Prices had also eased after the US and Iran reached a temporary agreement to halt attacks in June, although no permanent peace deal was reached.Brent has surged as high as $126.41 a barrel since the war began on February 28, reaching that peak on April 30. It briefly crossed $100 again in late July before falling back below the level.The International Energy Agency has forecast global oil supply to fall by 4.3 million barrels per day this year, or about 4%, adding to concerns over tighter supplies.The physical crude market is already reflecting the impact of supply disruptions. Dated Brent, a benchmark used to price around two-thirds of global oil supplies, has remained above $100 a barrel since September 3, according to LSEG data.Refined fuel prices have also remained elevated. US gasoline prices are averaging about $4.22 a gallon, while diesel prices are at record levels and approaching $6 a gallon.Higher crude prices could further raise the cost of gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, increasing transportation costs and pushing up prices of goods that rely on road, air or sea transport.Asian stocks fell on Thursday as oil prices stayed above $100, adding to investor concerns ahead of US inflation data that could influence the Federal Reserve's monetary policy.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures rose 0.1% to $101.34 a barrel by 0107 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 0.5%. Both benchmarks closed at their highest levels since May 22. Iran said it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz.

Article Title: Nitin Gadkari says he felt ‘ashamed’ at Mumbai-Goa highway work delays; ‘I want to set record of blacklisting maximum number of contractors and suspending officials for poor quality work’
Article Text:
He said the government would continue taking stringent action against contractors and officials responsible for delays and substandard execution of infrastructure projects.

‘Want to set record for blacklisting contractors, suspending officials’

Mumbai-Goa highway widening delayed

Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari has said that he wants to set a record blacklisting contractors who do poor quality work and also suspend officials.Gadkari said he had earlier expressed shame over the prolonged delay in widening the Mumbai-Goa Highway. He now plans to travel along the highway in October and personally review the work that has been completed.He was speaking after inaugurating a six-lane elevated road corridor at Porvorim near Panaji. Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant, Union Minister Shripad Naik, State Public Works Department Minister Digambar Kamat, Tourism Minister Rohan Khaunte and other officials were present at the event.Gadkari said on Wednesday that he wanted to "set a record" by blacklisting the largest possible number of contractors and suspending officials found responsible for delays or poor-quality execution in infrastructure projects."I had announced (earlier) that I would not come for the inauguration of the (widened) Mumbai-Goa highway because I felt ashamed that it had been delayed so much," he said.According to Gadkari, officials held a meeting on the issue on Tuesday."I would land at the Mumbai airport in October, and travel by road to Goa to personally inspect the highway and assess whether the journey has been made convenient for travellers," he said.The minister said the government would continue taking stringent action against contractors and officials responsible for delays and substandard execution of infrastructure projects."Now I want to set a record of blacklisting the maximum number of contractors and taking action against them, as well as suspending officials, within a year. I am not going to stop doing this now," he said.Gadkari also called on the Goa government to develop roadside amenities along the Mumbai-Goa highway that reflect the state's distinctive architecture, cuisine and handicraft traditions.He said these facilities should offer visitors an opportunity to experience Goan food and purchase the state's handloom and handicraft products, giving tourists a distinctive experience as they travel through Goa.Gadkari also proposed adding facilities for biofuels, electric vehicles and other alternative fuels alongside the petrol and diesel pumps operating on the route."If you make a request to me, I am ready to provide them to you," Gadkari said.The widening work on the Mumbai-Goa highway, which runs through Maharashtra's coastal Konkan region, has been delayed repeatedly.He also said landscaping along the highway should be planned scientifically rather than relying on contractors to carry out arbitrary tree plantation."Proper study should be conducted to determine which flowering trees and species should be planted, and which species absorb more carbon dioxide and release oxygen," the minister said.Gadkari appealed to Chief Minister Sawant and local MLAs to support efforts to turn the entire highway into a "green highway". He also suggested that it could be developed along the lines of an "oxygen park".The minister pointed out that he had previously developed an oxygen park in Nagpur.He said quality infrastructure covering water, electricity, transportation and communication is important for attracting investment, generating employment and helping reduce poverty.Gadkari further called for Goa to work towards eliminating water, air and noise pollution. He urged the authorities to ensure that waste does not find its way into the sea.He also sought a comprehensive review of traffic conditions in the state and reforms to address congestion. Among the measures he suggested were consolidating markets, relocating warehouses outside cities, upgrading bus depots and synchronising traffic movement.Referring to the newly inaugurated elevated corridor at Porvorim, Gadkari said a road that originally had a two-lane capacity now effectively provides capacity for ten lanes, with four lanes at ground level and six lanes on the elevated section.The minister also pushed for wider adoption of alternative fuels and technologies such as electric, hydrogen and flex-fuel systems, saying these would contribute to lowering pollution.
Article Summary: Gadkari said he had earlier expressed shame over the prolonged delay in widening the Mumbai-Goa Highway. He now plans to travel along the highway in October and personally review the work that has been completed. He was speaking after inaugurating a six-lane elevated road corridor at Porvorim near Panaji.

Article Title: Wall street suffers as crude tops $101 per barrel; Dow Jones tumbles over 300 points, Nasdaq down 0.6%
Article Text:
Wall street trades in red as crude tops $101 per barrel

Fuel costs add to inflation pressure

Investors await fresh inflation data

Oil's return above the $100-a-barrel mark pushed Wall Street lower on Wednesday, as the intensifying US-Iran conflict raised fresh concerns over fuel costs and inflation.Brent crude, the international benchmark, climbed 3.3% to $101.18 a barrel, crossing $100 for the first time since July. The move came after the US destroyed five Iranian tankers on Tuesday in a series of attacks between the two countries.The conflict, which began in February, has effectively brought traffic through the Strait of Hormuz to a halt. Before the war, the waterway carried a fifth of the world's oil supply.The rise in crude weighed on major US indices. The S&P 500 fell 37.04 points, or 0.48%, to 7,636.48. The Nasdaq declined 185.765 points, or 0.70%, to 26,235.647. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 389.86 points, or 0.74%, to 52,396.21.The decline was widespread, with retailers among the companies pulling the market lower. Amazon fell 1.8%, while Starbucks lost 1.5%. Nearly every sector of the S&P 500 was down. Oil companies, however, moved in the opposite direction, with Exxon Mobil gaining 1.9% and Chevron rising 1.6%.The latest jump in oil prices has added to inflationary pressure that had already been running high.US petrol prices are now about 32% above their level a year ago, at $4.22 a gallon.For households, higher petrol prices directly increase the cost of driving. They can also raise the prices of goods as businesses face higher shipping costs.Diesel prices have added to the pressure. Diesel, which is widely used in shipping and production, reached an all-time high on Friday and has continued to climb. Its average price reached $5.94 a gallon overnight, 9 cents higher than on Friday.Inflation was already proving stubborn before the US began its war against Iran, amid the continuing US trade war with much of the world. Trade tensions have also intensified, particularly between the US and Canada, a close US ally and trade partner.The focus will now turn to this week's inflation readings. Thursday's Producer Price Index for August will provide an indication of the prices businesses pay for goods before they reach consumers. The Consumer Price Index for August, due on Friday, will give a more direct picture of price pressures facing households.The latest reports are expected to show inflation remaining above 3%. That is still above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.The Fed has kept interest rates steady, but markets are increasingly factoring in a possible rate increase next week. Wall Street is pricing in a 60% chance of a hike at the central bank's meeting, according to CME Group data.Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive and are used to slow economic activity and bring inflation down.In the bond market, treasury yields were little changed. The 10-year Treasury yield edged up to 4.81% from 4.80% on Tuesday.
Article Summary: Brent crude, the international benchmark, climbed 3.3% to $101.18 a barrel. The move came after the US destroyed five Iranian tankers on Tuesday in a series of attacks between the two countries. The S&P 500 fell 37.04 points, or 0.48%, to 7,636.48.

Article Title: India’s exports grew over 15% in first five months of FY2026-27, says commerce minister Piyush Goyal
Article Text:
Merchandise exports rose 17.04% to $173.78 billion during April-July, while imports climbed 19.27% to $292.38 billion.

Three hurdles for businesses

Push for common BRICS trade infrastructure

India’s merchandise exports have grown by more than 15 per cent in the first five months of the current fiscal despite a challenging global trade environment, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Wednesday.The union minister said the growth highlighted the potential for India and other BRICS economies to deepen trade in goods and services, particularly as businesses navigate geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions and uncertainty.“Despite all the turmoil that the world is going through today...I am happy to share that our merchandise exports from India have grown between April and August, in the first five months of this fiscal, by upward of 15 per cent,” Goyal said at the Brics Women’s Business Alliance (WBA) Women-Led Development Summit 2026, as quoted by PTI.Official trade data for August is due on September 15. In the April-July period, merchandise exports rose 17.04% to $173.78 billion, while imports increased 19.27 per cent to $292.38 billion.Goyal said expanding international trade would require Brics countries to address three key challenges faced by businesses — access to finance, access to buyers and markets, and predictable rules for doing business.He called for greater support for women entrepreneurs and small businesses, including easier access to credit and more opportunities to participate in international trade events.“If we can commit our governments to encourage women-owned enterprises to take greater part in international expositions, conferences, seminars, exhibitions, business forums, it will actually help us engage on many more platforms than an annual Women Business Alliance meeting,” he said.Goyal also proposed more sector-specific women-led business delegations between BRICS countries, giving the example of a women-led textile delegation travelling from one member country to another.The minister pointed to the Jaipur Consensus, agreed upon at the BRICS Commerce and Industry Ministers’ meeting last month, which includes exploring a common BRICS platform for international trade.Such a platform, he said, could help businesses find buyers and enter new markets, while financial intermediaries could provide support to women entrepreneurs and small businesses.Goyal also pushed for greater digital integration in trade, suggesting that BRICS members work towards a common system for electronic trade documents, including e-invoices, electronic bills of lading and e-customs declarations.He said countries should also facilitate cross-border delivery of services online while continuing to respect their respective laws.Goyal said services could also provide another major avenue for expanding intra-BRICS trade. With global services trade approaching $10 trillion, he said the relatively low level of services trade within BRICS points to significant untapped potential.Women entrepreneurs and MSMEs, he said, could play a larger role in areas including mobility, services and the digital economy On financing, Goyal asked the BRICS Women’s Business Alliance and BRICS Business Council to ensure that a proposed study on an invoice discounting platform addresses the actual needs of women exporters.He also urged governments, banks and Exim Banks to consider such invoices while taking lending decisions and called for the proposed Women’s Advancement Fund under the Jaipur Consensus to be turned into a concrete initiative.Goyal said closer cooperation among BRICS economies was important at a time of heightened volatility and uncertainty in global trade, while emphasising that the bloc should continue engaging with the wider global economy.
Article Summary: India’s merchandise exports have grown by more than 15 per cent in the first five months of the current fiscal. In the April-July period, merchandise exports rose 17.04% to $173.78 billion, while imports increased 19.27 per cent to $292.38 billion. Official trade data for August is due on September 15.

Article Title: Billion dollar boom: Jefferies identifies six sectors driving ‘India’s New Industrial Revolution’
Article Text:
Jefferies has identified semiconductors, space, electronics, solar, aerospace and data centres as the top 6 themes.

India’s next phase of industrial growth: Which sectors will drive it?

Jefferies has identified semiconductors, space, electronics, solar, aerospace and data centres as the top 6 themes. Let’s take a look:

Electronics:

Space:

Semiconductors:

Aerospace:

Data Centres:

Solar:

Global investment bank Jefferies, in its latest report ‘India’s New Industrial Revolution’, has highlighted sectors that are poised for growth due to a combination of India's large domestic market, greater participation from private companies and continued government policy support.Jefferies has identified several policy measures that it believes are helping these newer sectors expand, driving India’s next phase of industrial growth. These include allowing greater private-sector participation in space, providing tax holidays for data centres, offering incentives for semiconductors, electronics and solar, promoting localisation and government purchases of GPUs.According to Jefferies, India's electronics industry is gradually shifting beyond basic assembly. There is now greater emphasis on domestic value addition and component manufacturing. Domestic value addition in mobile components is expected to increase from below 20% to around 50% over the next 6 years.“Electronics exports have grown sharply, while schemes such as ECMS (components scheme) and MPMS (Mobile 2.0) aim to deepen backward integration and reduce import dependence. We forecast ECMS to cover ~50% of Mobile component value (BoM) over the next 6-Y vs <20% now.PCB (both HDI + Multi-layer) is a focus area for Components, with $5bn TAM, 85-90% imports,” says Jefferies.Jefferies has that India is one of the few countries with spacefaring capabilities that are competitive globally. The country's space economy is expected to expand nearly fivefold to $40–45 billion by 2030. Private companies including Skyroot, Pixxel and Agnikul are also progressing towards commercial execution.“The government opened the sector for private participation in 2020, and is targeting ~5x expansion of space economy over 2023-30 to $40-45bn. Startups are advancing from early innovation to commercial execution with companies such as Skyroot (orbital launch in July), Pixxel (high-res observation satellites), Agnikul (3D-printed rocket engine) & Digantara (surveillance satellites),” the report said.India's semiconductor ambitions are now moving beyond policy announcements towards actual execution. Investment of around $20 billion is underway, with a chip fabrication plant under construction and several OSAT projects beginning production. Another incentive package of around $13 billion is expected to further strengthen the semiconductor ecosystem.“While supply chain depth, talent, and global competition remain challenges, we believe India is building the foundations of a credible semiconductor ecosystem,” Jefferies says.India is increasingly positioned to benefit from the mismatch between global aerospace demand and supply, helped by cost-competitive manufacturing and engineering talent.Boeing and Airbus currently source $1.4–1.6 billion annually from India, while Indian companies are also supplying global OEMs and Tier-1 companies.“Indian companies such as Aezad, BHFC, DYTC, RW, MOTHERSON & SANSERA have become suppliers to global OEMs and tier-1s, and are expanding in the segment,” it notes.India's data centre capacity has increased fivefold over the past five years to around 2 GW. Jefferies expects this to rise to approximately 10 GW over the coming five years, translating into a $45 billion investment opportunity spanning power, cooling, construction and network infrastructure.India has become the world's second-largest solar PV manufacturer. Around 35 GW of cell manufacturing capacity is currently operational, while another approximately 100 GW is under construction. Jefferies expects around 90% of the solar value chain to be localised by 2030.
Article Summary: Jefferies has identified semiconductors, space, electronics, solar, aerospace and data centres as the top 6 themes for India’s next phase of industrial growth. The country's space economy is expected to expand nearly fivefold to $40–45 billion by 2030. India is increasingly positioned to benefit from the mismatch between global aerospace demand and supply.

Article Title: 'Largest Europe investment': Google to invest nearly $15 billion in AI Infrastructure in Finland
Article Text:
"Google's decision is a clear testament to our strengths," Finland's Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a statement (Photo: Reuters).

Google announced to invest 13 billion euros (nearly $15.1 billion) in Finland in the next two years, on Monday, its largest investment in Europe."This is Google's largest single investment in Europe and a testament to Finland's leadership in responsibly building AI infrastructure," the company said on Wednesday, stating that Google is proud to deepen its roots in Finland.The investment package would include three new data centres in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala in the northern part of the country; expansion of an existing site in the southeastern city of Hamina; and support for energy projects to power the centres.According to Google, the sites were selected to take advantage of existing grid infrastructure near carbon-free energy sources.Finland has a relatively cold climate and is preferred for setting up data centres. According to Bloomberg, the heat generated by the servers in the data centres can be captured to warm up homes, as the centres will reportedly possess heat recovery readiness.Additionally, nearly 96 per cent of electricity in the country is produced from nuclear or renewable sources.Data centres need fresh water, which Finland has plenty of. The country developed a closed-loop system that reduces water waste.Google has also signed a 22-year contract with Finland’s state-owned ‘Fortum’ to buy up to 50 per cent of the electricity output from the Loviisa nuclear power plant.The company is also expanding the energy infrastructure with wind-power agreements and a 94-megawatt battery system at the Kajaani site to help balance the grid.According to Google’s estimates, the project will support more than 37,000 jobs during the building phase, including around 16,000 in construction. After completion, the facilities will support 7,000 jobs, including suppliers and local services."Google's decision is a clear testament to our strengths," Finland's Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a statement.For Finland, the investment provides a significant boost as the Nordic country seeks to revive economic growth. Finland has been grappling with weak demand, the collapse in trade with neighbouring Russia and the impact of fiscal tightening aimed at bringing public finances under control. Its unemployment rate has risen above 10 per cent, the highest in the European Union.The move also forms part of Alphabet’s efforts to accelerate the expansion of its AI computing capacity. The Silicon Valley giant raised its capital spending forecast in July to as much as $205 billion for this year, as it competes with rivals to establish dominance in the AI landscape.
Article Summary: Google announced to invest 13 billion euros (nearly $15.1 billion) in Finland in the next two years. The investment package would include three new data centres in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala in the northern part of the country. The Silicon Valley giant raised its capital spending forecast in July to as much as $205 billion for this year.

Article Title: Woman had gold, diamond jewellery and silver in her home and locker; tax department seized them, but ITAT deletes Rs 11.23 lakh additions - how she won the case
Article Text:
The Income Tax Department seized all these items and the Assessing Officer (AO) asked the woman to produce bills. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

During the search of her house, Income Tax officials found the following items:

Gold jewellery - 392.71 grams

Pure gold - 92 grams

27.4 carats of diamond jewellery containing 161.33 grams of gold

800 grams of silver items and coins

The search of her bank lockers resulted in the recovery of:

166 grams (81+85 grams) of pure gold

10.4 kg (10 kg + 400 grams) of silver mixed articles

35 grams of gold jewellery

What the Income Tax Department said

How did the woman win the case?

What ITAT Mumbai said:

Silver articles

Shri Dinkar Laxman Mujumdar v. DCIT

Pure gold

A woman, who has been married for 35 years and lives with her husband in Navi Mumbai, found herself caught up in a tax dispute over jewellery that was seized by the Income Tax Department . She eventually approached the ITAT Mumbai to seek the return of the gold, diamond and silver items seized during the department's search operation.The matter began after the woman filed her income tax return (ITR) on August 12, 2019, declaring an income of Rs 1.34 lakh. However, around a year before she filed the return, the Income Tax Department came across information about her while conducting a search at the offices of a company.Based on the information it had received, the department suspected that the woman was in possession of several high-value gold, diamond and silver jewellery items. It subsequently issued her multiple tax notices and also conducted searches at her residence and bank lockers.The Income Tax Department seized all these items and the Assessing Officer (AO) asked the woman to produce bills and other supporting evidence to establish their ownership and source.In response, the woman explained that she had been married for 35 years and that part of the jewellery had been received as gifts from relatives at the time of her marriage. She said other pieces formed part of her inheritance and streedhan. Her husband also stated that he had disclosed income of Rs 4 crore in his ITR and had occasionally gifted jewellery to his wife, including a gold chain given to her recently, ET reported.The AO was not fully convinced by this explanation. He referred to Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) Instruction No. 1916 and held that the woman was entitled to retain a total of 700 grams of jewellery, which includes 500 grams for a married woman and 100 grams each for her husband and son.The quantity beyond this limit was treated as unexplained under Section 69A by the AO.The AO consequently assessed Rs 19.4 lakh as unexplained income and imposed tax on the amount, along with a penalty. The woman challenged the assessment before the Commissioner of Appeals (CIT A).The CIT (A) partly allowed her appeal but upheld the remaining additions. She then took the matter to the ITAT Mumbai, where she secured a complete victory on July 14, 2026.Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana explains why the ITAT Mumbai ruled in the woman’s favour and removed the remaining additions totalling Rs 11.23 lakh.Surana told ET that the key reason the woman succeeded was that she was able to explain how she came to possess the different gold, diamond and silver items.Her explanation was that the jewellery and other articles had been accumulated over a long period and acquired through customary family practices, which was consistent with the circumstances of the family. The Income Tax Department, however, did not bring any contrary material to establish that the assets had been recently acquired using undisclosed income.The ITAT Mumbai therefore deleted the addition of Rs 8.1 lakh relating to pure gold and another Rs 3.12 lakh concerning silver articles. The two additions amounted to Rs 11,23,190 in total, and the woman’s appeal was allowed.Surana also pointed out that the tribunal specifically limited its finding concerning pure gold to the facts of this particular case.The decision, therefore, should not be understood as establishing a general rule that every holding of gold bullion or pure gold automatically receives the benefit of CBDT Instruction No. 1916.On the silver articles, Surana said the tribunal considered the circumstances in which such items were held instead of insisting that the woman produce old purchase invoices for them.The ITAT Mumbai referred to the Indore ITAT decision in, where the benefit of CBDT Instruction No. 1916 had similarly been extended to silver articles.Taking into account the woman’s long marriage, the customary receipt of silver articles at the time of marriage and on other family occasions, inheritance and the family's financial standing, the tribunal concluded that the silver articles could reasonably be treated as explained.The tribunal dealt separately with 258 grams of pure gold. It clarified that CBDT Instruction No. 1916 does not, by itself, grant automatic immunity to every quantity of pure gold or bullion. At the same time, the instruction can provide a reasonable reference point when assessing the gold held by a family.The tribunal first excluded 195.996 grams of gold jewellery for which purchase bills were available. After this exclusion, the remaining gold, comprising ordinary jewellery, the gold component in the diamond jewellery and pure gold, came to 651.044 grams.According to Surana, the ITAT observed that this quantity remained within the 700-gram family benchmark that the AO himself had accepted by applying the CBDT Instruction.The tribunal also found it difficult to justify a distinction within the same family holding by accepting ordinary gold jewellery and diamond-studded gold jewellery while treating the pure gold as unexplained simply because it was held in a different physical form.More importantly, Surana said the ITAT Mumbai found that neither the AO nor the CIT(A) had produced any evidence showing that the pure gold had been acquired afresh during the relevant year using undisclosed income.The fact that old purchase invoices were unavailable was therefore not considered sufficient, on its own, to reject the woman’s explanation, particularly when her explanation was based on marriage gifts, inheritance and assets accumulated over several decades.The tribunal's decision also makes clear that CBDT Instruction No. 1916 is not an absolute tax exemption or a statutory upper limit on the amount of jewellery that can be held.Surana says “the quantities specified in the instruction provide a practical benchmark for assessing whether family possession of jewellery can reasonably be accepted as explained.”Such an assessment, according to the ruling, has to consider factors including the taxpayer's length of marriage, family customs, inheritance, streedhan, social and financial status and other surrounding circumstances.The ITAT Mumbai consequently held that an addition under Section 69A cannot be upheld merely because purchase invoices are unavailable for assets that have been accumulated over several decades, especially when there is no evidence showing that those assets were acquired from undisclosed income during the relevant year.
Article Summary: A woman, who has been married for 35 years and lives with her husband in Navi Mumbai, found herself caught up in a tax dispute over jewellery that was seized by the Income Tax Department. She eventually approached the ITAT Mumbai to seek the return of the gold, diamond and silver items seized during the department's search operation. The matter began after the woman filed her income tax return on August 12, 2019, declaring an income of Rs 1.34 lakh.

Bringing the D’LIFE experience to Noida and Gurugram

A 350,000 Sq. Ft. manufacturing facility behind the experience

From concept to completion

Designed for confidence beyond handover

A new chapter in NCR

Article Title: LVX, Nqbator sign pact to build India-UAE private markets corridor
Article Text:
Bengaluru:

Sebi-regulated private markets platform LVX has signed an MoU with Dubai-based startup incubator Nqubator to build a cross-border bridge connecting founders and investors in India and the UAE.The partnership will include the launch of LVX Corridor, an initiative aimed at facilitating two-way movement of startups and capital between the two markets.Under the non-binding agreement, the organisations will work on mentorship and advisory programmes, joint events and demo days, and introductions among startups, investors and ecosystem partners.The initiative focuses on startups in digital commerce, retail technology, logistics, supply chain and the circular economy. It offers mentorship, corporate pilot opportunities and investor-readiness support. Startups that attract investor interest will be eligible for an investment opportunity of up to $1 million.LVX said the Corridor will initially help Indian startups access Dubai’s ecosystem, including regulatory navigation across Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) and Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM), while providing a base for expansion into the wider Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) market.The initiative will also give GCC-based founders access to India’s investor and deal ecosystem. LVX plans to support investor education, syndicate structures and alternative investment fund (AIF) structures to help channel UAE private wealth into Indian startups.The initiative will be rolled out over 24 months, beginning with ecosystem entry and regulatory groundwork in the first six months. LVX expects to facilitate the first syndicated deals with UAE high-net-worth individuals and family offices by the 12th month, followed by a more institutionalised cross-border deal marketplace by the end of the second year.The partnership comes as startup funding in the MENA region reached a record $7.5 billion in 2025, according to LVX. The company said its India network includes more than 35,000 registered investors, over 5,000 AIF investors and 715 funded portfolio companies. Its AI platform, ELVIX, analyses deals across more than 320 data points.“It took us twelve years to build the infrastructure that turns Indian wealth into startup capital—the deal flow, the syndication, the investor education, and now an AI layer that scores every deal,” said Shanti Mohan, founder and CEO, LVX. “The UAE has the capital and the founders; what’s been missing is the infrastructure connecting the two.”Sultan Rashed Ali Lootah, chairman, Nqubator, said the partnership would connect Dubai’s digital commerce ecosystem with global innovation hubs, with LVX’s private-markets expertise and India network supporting relationships across founders, corporates and investors.
Article Summary: Sebi-regulated private markets platform LVX has signed an MoU with Dubai-based startup incubator Nqubator. The partnership will include the launch of LVX Corridor, an initiative aimed at facilitating two-way movement of startups and capital between the two markets.

Article Title: RBI flags tech concentration risks, warns of disruptions
Article Text: MUMBAI: RBI deputy governor Rohit Jain flagged concentration risk among banks as most of them become dependent on a few cloud, technology and model providers, warning that a common technology dependency could allow a disruption at one provider to spread across multiple financial institutions.Speaking at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai on Wednesday, Jain said emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, tokenisation, distributed technologies and quantum computing could make finance cheaper, more accessible and responsive, but could also amplify risks by increasing the speed, scale and interconnectedness of financial systems."I see three key concerns as emerging technologies become more deeply embedded in finance: speed, concentration and opacity," Jain said. "None of these risks is entirely new, but technology can amplify them and allow their effects to travel through the financial system in ways that are faster, wider and sometimes harder to detect."On concentration, Jain said financial institutions could increasingly rely on a relatively small number of cloud providers, technology vendors and model providers, often using overlapping datasets and similar infrastructure. This, he said, meant that the failure of a common provider could become a financial-system problem rather than an isolated institutional failure. "The concern is therefore not simply the failure of one institution, but the possibility that a common dependency could transmit disruption or error across many institutions at the same time," he said."An institution may outsource the computation, but it cannot outsource the consequence," he said, adding: "Technology also does not eliminate traditional risks."
Article Summary: RBI deputy governor Rohit Jain flagged concentration risk among banks. Most of them become dependent on a few cloud, technology and model providers. He warned that a common technology dependency could allow a disruption at one provider to spread across multiple financial institutions.

Article Title: Coforge stock tumbles 6% as chairman Bhatt resigns
Article Text: BENGALURU: Coforge shares dropped nearly 6% on BSE after chairman and independent director OP Bhatt resigned from the company's board with immediate effect on Tuesday. The resignation followed an internal audit review that raised concerns about how the company's board evaluation exercise was handled and presented. Bhatt became chairman of Coforge in 2024. He previously served as chairman of State Bank of India from 2006 to 2011.Coforge said the internal audit, conducted as part of its plan for the Sept quarter of FY26, identified concerns relating to the Board Evaluation Report (BER). These included the non-disclosure of certain material information relating to the report and the chairman's performance when it was presented to the board.The board subsequently raised its concerns with Bhatt and sought an explanation. While Bhatt responded, the board was still evaluating his explanation and had not taken any final decision when he resigned on Sept 8."The Board considers it important to clarify that the chairman's resignation followed the concerns identified in the internal audit review and the subsequent process undertaken by the Board to seek and consider his explanation," Coforge said in its regulatory filing.In his resignation email, Bhatt said he had considered the matters raised concerning the board evaluation process and the circumstances that followed."I believe that continuing on the Board while there remains a disagreement considering the characteristics of my good faith actions in the Board evaluation process would not be conducive to the effective functioning of the Board," Bhatt said.He added that the matters relating to the board evaluation process were the material reasons for his resignation and that there were no other material reasons. Bhatt said he had served as an independent director and chairman with a "strong sense of responsibility" and had sought to discharge his duties independently and objectively, while balancing the interests of shareholders, management and the company.Coforge has designated non-executive independent director Vivek Sharma as interim chairperson until Jan 31, 2027. Bhatt will also cease to be a member of the company's board committees with immediate effect.The resignation follows a shareholder vote last month in which investors rejected Bhatt's reappointment as an independent director. At the company's 34th annual general meeting on Aug 24, the special resolution received 65.4% votes in favour and 34.5% against, failing to secure the required majority. "It looks like disagreements on strategy and policy matters between the chairman and the largest shareholder, Advent, seem to have led to this resignation."The reappointment of OP Bhatt effective May 2027 put to vote at the Aug 24 AGM was voted against, with Advent, the largest shareholder voting against," said Shriram Subramanian, MD of corporate governance research firm InGovern Research Services.
Article Summary: Coforge shares dropped nearly 6% on BSE after chairman and independent director OP Bhatt resigned. resignation followed an internal audit review that raised concerns about how the company's board evaluation exercise was handled and presented. Bhatt previously served as chairman of State Bank of India from 2006 to 2011.

Article Title: Sensex tanks 813 points as crude spikes
Article Text: MUMBAI: Rising geopolitical tensions in the Persian Gulf region pushed up Brent prices above the $100-per-barrel mark for the first time since July on Wednesday. This, in turn, led to the weakening of the rupee, which fell below the 95/$ mark and settled at 95.1 at close. Dalal Street, too, felt the jitters courtesy of these developments, with investors pressing the sell button, resulting in sensex falling below the 75K mark after nearly three months.With foreign funds selling aggressively, the benchmark index closed 813 points lower at 74,764 points. HDFC Bank and Infosys contributed the most to the day's losses. On NSE, Nifty lost 204 points (0.9%) to close at 23,432 points.In the last one month, sensex has lost nearly 3,800 points or 4.8%, while Nifty is down 1,152 points or 4.7%. The losses came on the back of muted foreign fund activity through this one-month period. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), however, have again turned aggressive sellers in Sept. After two months of net inflows, FPIs have net sold stocks worth around Rs 12,400 crore in India, so far this month, combined data from NSDL and BSE showed.A revival in Chinese demand for crude also helped the rally in oil prices, reports said.Bond yields in US, where the yield on the 10-year Treasury (govt) bonds crossed the 4.8%-per-annum mark again, led market players to believe there's a high chance it may soon move closer to the 5% mark, adding to the worry of investors.Against this backdrop-rising oil prices which could stoke inflation and rising bond yields-US Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting next week, with its rate decision set for Sept 16, is turning out to be an extremely important one for the market. Any indication of a rate hike in US could have global implications, market players here said.According to Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments, markets are increasingly pricing in a prolonged West Asia conflict, with continued hostilities and retaliatory actions expected to keep crude oil prices elevated in the near term. "Persistent geopolitical uncertainty is making it difficult for major central banks to achieve a balance between growth and inflation," he said.On the sectoral front, software services stocks led the slide. "The Nifty IT index declined around 3%, as rising US bond yields, concerns over US Federal Reserve's rate outlook and structural worries around AI-driven disruption weighed on technology stocks," said Ajit Mishra of Religare Broking. "Realty, financials and FMCG also edged lower, while select defence, metal and energy-related stocks showed relative resilience. "
Article Summary: Rising geopolitical tensions in the Persian Gulf region pushed up Brent prices above the $100-per-barrel mark for the first time since July. This, in turn, led to the weakening of the rupee, which fell below the 95/$ mark and settled at 95.1 at close. HDFC Bank and Infosys contributed the most to the day's losses.

Article Title: Cognizant's green card filings suspended amid probe by US
Article Text: BENGALURU: Cognizant's US green-card filings have been suspended amid an investigation into potential fraud and misuse of employment visa programmes, Anthony D'Esposito, inspector general at US Department of Labor, said in a post on X. "Fighting fraud is a Team Sport.....Threats to American workers will not be tolerated. Alongside @WHFraudTF, we're following facts, fraud and finances. Handcuffs await," he posted on X.The move could further complicate the immigration outlook for Cognizant's foreign employees, many of whom already face prolonged waits and uncertainty over obtaining permanent residency and, eventually, citizenship in US. It could also raise questions among clients about how the company will staff projects requiring specialised skills if the suspension affects the movement or long-term status of foreign workers.Companies generally do not disclose how many employees have received US green cards or how many are currently in the green-card sponsorship process, making it difficult to assess the number of workers directly affected by the suspension.The suspension comes a day after Cognizant announced plans to hire 1,500 US college graduates and expand its frontier certified engineer and frontier business operator workforce to 15,000 people.In July, US Department of Labor launched a nationwide investigation into alleged fraud involving the H-1B and PERM employment visa programmes.
Article Summary: Cognizant's US green-card filings have been suspended amid an investigation into potential fraud and misuse of employment visa programmes. The move could further complicate the immigration outlook for the company's foreign employees. It could also raise questions among clients about how the company will staff projects requiring specialised skills.

Article Title: Meta officials appear before NCPCR
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Senior executives from Meta India, appeared before National Commission for Protection of Child Rights Wednesday in connection with the inquiry instituted to investigate the allegations linked to circulation of child sexual exploitative abuse material (CSEAM) on Instagram The details of those present from Meta and the questioning and cross-examination that would have followed were not shared by NCPCR till the time of going to the press. The commission had summoned the MD and head of Meta India to appear before it 3pm Wednesday.Additional secretary in the ministry of women and child development, who is holding additional charge as NCPCR chairperson, Valeti Premchand, led the hearing. Member secretary Sanjeev Sharma and ministry of electronics and information technology officials were also present. NCPCR had issued a notice to Meta on July 3 taking suo moto cognisance of a BBC report alleging advertisements related to CSEAM on its platform.
Article Summary: Senior executives from Meta India, appeared before National Commission for Protection of Child Rights Wednesday. NCPCR had issued a notice to Meta on July 3 taking suo moto cognisance of a BBC report alleging advertisements related to CSEAM on its platform.

Article Title: OMCs may be losing Rs 5/L on petrol, Rs 23 on diesel: ICRA
Article Text:
OMCs may be losing Rs 5/L on petrol, Rs 23 on diesel: ICRA

NEW DELHI: A surge in global crude prices due to renewed hostilities has started hitting the oil marketing companies, with state-owned fuel retailers estimated to be losing around Rs 5 per litre on petrol and Rs 23 on diesel, ratings agency ICRA said Wednesday.Oil retailers refused to comment on the exact amount of under-recoveries. While Indian basket of crude oil reached $108.91 Tuesday, the highest since May 21, Brent breached the $100-mark Wednesday and was trading at $101.23 a barrel at 8.30pm The last time Brent had breached the $100-per-barrel mark was July 23.Industry players said under-recoveries on petrol, diesel and domestic LPG cylinders may rise further if crude prices remain elevated for a longer duration and retail pump prices remain unchanged. Oil retailers were making an under-recovery of more than Rs 1,000 crore a day during the peak of the conflict in April and May, when Indian basket of crude oil averaged more than $110 per barrel.
Article Summary: State-owned fuel retailers estimated to be losing around Rs 5 per litre on petrol and Rs 23 on diesel. Indian basket of crude oil reached $108.91 Tuesday, the highest since May 21. Brent breached the $100-mark Wednesday and was trading at $101.23 a barrel at 8.30pm.

Article Title: NSE cuts IPO size, may raise 23.5k crore
Article Text: MUMBAI: IPO-bound National Stock Exchange (NSE), the largest stock exchange in India by turnover and profits, is reducing the size of its offering to about 5.3% of its equity base, from 6% planned earlier. The stocks will be offered in a price band of Rs 1,700 to Rs 1,785 per share, people in the know said.In effect, the reduced size and also the price band would together cut the offer size to about Rs 23,500 crore. Earlier, NSE's IPO was expected to raise about Rs 30,000 crore, which would have made it the largest current public listing in India.According to people in the know, even during pre-IPO days when NSE management was persuading its shareholders to offer their shares in the IPO, very few were willing to sell their stakes in the offer. They were willing to hold on to the shares, see the post-IPO price on the bourse and once the lock-in was to end, decide about their holdings, a source said.At the upper end of the reduced price band, NSE would be valued at about Rs 4.4 lakh crore, down from an earlier estimate of about Rs 5 lakh crore.On Sept 4, markets regulator Sebi cleared NSE's IPO documents. Earlier, existing shareholders together were selling nearly 15 crore shares, which is now being reduced to about 13.2 crore shares.Market participants said the offer would be launched "as soon as possible". And according to merchant banking sources, the offer could open as soon as Sept 16.Currently, in the unofficial space for trading of shares, NSE is quoting between Rs 1,950 and Rs 2,050. In the same market, the grey market premium (GMP)-the estimated premium that the share could command at listing-has been fluctuating over the last few days.
Article Summary: IPO-bound National Stock Exchange (NSE) is reducing the size of its offering to about 5.3% of its equity base, from 6% planned earlier. The reduced size and also the price band would together cut the offer size to about Rs 23,500 crore. Earlier, NSE's IPO was expected to raise about Rs 30,000 crore.
